chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abi Walad, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, and others from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in the wage of the broker. He only purchases for people day after day for a specified amount. He is only like a hired worker.

key_terms.أَجْرِ: wage or compensation for work performed
key_terms.السِّمْسَارِ: broker or intermediary who buys or arranges transactions for others
key_terms.الْأَجِيرِ: a hired worker who lawfully receives wages
key_terms.بِشَيْءٍ مُسَمًّى: for a specified and known payment

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to take a broker's fee for buying goods on behalf of others?
ai.summary: This hadith states that taking payment for brokerage is permissible. It explains that the broker performs ongoing purchasing work for others for a known compensation, and is therefore treated like a hired worker.
